title: Trade easing will support recovery in global economy: Morgan Stanley chief economist
description: Jeff Krumpelman, Mariner Wealth Advisors head of equities, and Chetan Ahya, Morgan Stanley global chief economist, join "The Exchange" to discuss if the markets could reach new level highs.   Receive exclusive commentary from CNBC anchor Kelly Evans: https://cnb.cx/2CWYubi  » Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC  About CNBC: From 'Wall Street' to 'Main Street' to award winning original documentaries and Reality TV series, CNBC has you covered. Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more. asr.full_text: But that means only another hundred points left on your prediction. So is it over? You know we actually established those targets back in December when everyone thought we were headed to you know recession and worse. Zero. Right exactly. So blood pressures relieved a little bit and at this point I'd say the bias is maybe to take that up to higher levels. If I would have said you know above 3,000 back then I think they would have, you know burned my house down. People were so grumpy. So, we do think the backdrop is favorable. The fundamentals are very favorable. So, instead of 3,000, potentially, where do we go, potentially? I think, you know, 3,000, if you put a normal handle of 16, 16.5, 17 times on 7% growth in earnings over the, you know, 2019, 20 time frame, it gets you to that 3000 and a little bit above. So, for multiples to lift a little bit in a low inflationary environment, with these good fundamentals, you could you know go to 31, 3200, comfortably I would think. But it's really about trend, Tyler. Get the trend. I would say, we're still there. Chetan, what do you see in the economy that either heartens you or worries you? We think that the economy is going to recover from here. First quarter 2019 will be the trough in global growth. We see it recovering from 3.2, to 3.5 which is going back to trend and we think it's the easing trial which is going to help, which is essentially trade tensions easing, we have China policy easing, and we have Fed's flexibility-on-policy approach. So these three factors, we think, will drive that global recovery. Mind you, these were the three problems that we were facing in the fourth quarter of last year, and we have visibility now that all the three factors will actually support this recovery. We will think that we think that this will be driven more by the rest of the world than the USA. So the recovery in the rest of the world is going to be even more prominent. It will go from the trough of three point three to three point nine. That's a meaningful rebound that you should see in the global growth in parts of the world other than the US. And so you see a change in the trade outlook as IN THE GLOBAL GROWTH, IN PARTS OF THE WORLD OTHER THAN THE U.S. RICK KINSEY. AND SO YOU SEE A CHANGE IN THE TRADE OUTLOOK AS CRITICAL TO THAT. THAT MEANS EUROPE, I ASSUME, AND CHINA? Y.A. ESSENTIALLY BEING FROM A DEMAND PERSPECTIVE GOING TO BE DRIVEN BY CHINA, BUT FROM A POLICY PERSPECTIVE, IT IS THE U.S. AND CHINA TRADE TENSIONS THAT IS A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF THIS STORY. WE THINK IN CHINA'S CASE IT'S NOT JUST TRADE TENSION EASING trade tensions that is a critical component of this story. And we think that in China's case, it's not just trade tensions easing that will help its recovery, but the stimulus that has been laid out by the government so far seems quite sizable. It's 1.75 percent of GDP, or call it $250 billion. We think that's a sizable stimulus that will help recovery in China. We should get that data confirming tomorrow that China's recovery is actually taking hold in the month of March itself.

The discussion includes market levels, earnings growth, and economic forecasts, but no promoted investment product, guaranteed return, required payment, credential request, or other audience-directed financial transaction. The visible CNBC subscribe prompt is ordinary channel engagement and is not linked to a financial offer.
